messages:
alex: FYI — I kicked off a small upgrade matrix across the staging GPU fleet last night (kernel/driver/firmware combos). Quick thread to capture findings and a proposed gating rule.

alex: Test plan: 12 nodes (3 zones), 24h steady transformer inference load + periodic stress-ng mem test, collect dmesg, nvidia-smi ECC counters, and our xid telemetry.

mira: Nice. Which combos did you run?

alex: matrix entries (condensed):
- kernel: 6.5.3 (lts), 6.4.21 (customer LTS)
- driver: nvidia/535.104.05, nvidia/540.86.01
- fw: GPUFW v48, v50 (vendor labels)

alex: Command snippets I used:
```
# ECC counters snapshot
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,ecc.errors.volatile.uncorrected --format=csv
# look for NVRM/Xid in kernel logs
journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "24 hours ago" | grep -i -E "NVRM|Xid"
```

jordan: Summary first — did any combo look worse?

alex: Most combos were neutral. Driver 540 + fw v50 on kernel 6.5.3 had 3 Xid events across two nodes (same rack) during a memstress window. Same workload on 535+v48 had 0-1 Xid. ECC raw counts stayed within baseline except one GPU with rising correctable ECC on channel 2.

ryan: Rack-level — could be power or PCI riser. Did you see correlated PCIe AER logs?

alex: Good call. That problematic node shows repeated AER: "Device reset, link down" entries just before Xid. Stack of logs:
```
[ 12345.678901] pcieport 0000:3c:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received
[ 12345.679123] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3c:00): 79, GPU is lost
```

mira: So maybe it's hardware sensitivity to newer driver/fw combo. Did you repro by swapping driver only?

alex: I re-ran the exact node with driver 535 + fw v50 (so only driver older) — no Xids in 6h smoke. Then driver 540 + fw v48 showed 1 Xid in 6h. So pattern points to driver 540 as the likely trigger, amplified by either fw v50 or existing flaky PCIe.

jordan: What do we want as a gating rule for rolling to production?

alex: Proposal:
- Gate: no more than 2 Xid events per fleet per 24h across canary pool (size configurable).
- Any AER/PCIe resets on a node during canary -> node removed and hardware flagged for diagnostics (drain+replace after retest).
- Driver upgrade to 540 only if 72h canary across 20 nodes with <2 Xid and no AERs.
- Automated rollback hook if Xid rate exceeds baseline by 3x in production traffic for 1h.

ryan: Agree but tweak numbers: make Xid threshold per-GPU rather than per-fleet. e.g., >1 Xid per GPU in 24h fails. That catches single flaky cards.

mira: Also add telemetry check: if correctable ECC increases >10x over baseline for any GPU during canary, fail upgrade.

alex: Updated: per-GPU Xid >1/24h OR AER present -> fail. ECC increase >10x -> fail. Rollback hook exists in the deploy job (`deploy/gpu-driver/rollforward`) — I added a check that queries /telemetry/xid_rate.

sre-bot: ALERT: deploy/gpu-driver/rollforward job updated with canary checks by alex at 1893456882 :eyes:

jordan: What's the mitigation plan for the flagged rack? Do we drain and replace immediately or swap riser?

alex: For now: drain workloads, repro with 535+v48 to confirm hardware; if Xid persists on 535 -> hardware replacement. If Xid goes away on 535 -> treat as driver incompatibility, escalate to vendor and hold on production rollout.

mira: Can someone add the per-node repro logs to the ticket in infra/bugzilla-579?

ryan: I'll attach dmesg, nvidia-smi dumps, and AER traces by EOD. Also scheduling an overnight 48h run with the suspect node under 535/540 combos and toggled fw v48/v50.

alex: Thanks — I'll update the canary runbook with these gating criteria and link to the rollback script. If we get a clean 48h on 20 nodes, we can promote driver 540 in limited prod (non-latency critical pools) next week.

mira: :thumbsup: please ping #oncall when you start the 48h so they can watch Xid alerts.

sre-bot: Reminder sent to @oncall at 1893456895

alex: will do. Thanks all.
